title: Which Zscaler products stage changes behind an activation
aliases: why is my change not taking effect

prose.text: Whether a product stages a saved change until someone activates it decides whether an ignored change is an activation question at all. The OneAPI guide names ZIA and Cloud & Branch Connector, and says a queued activation cannot be cancelled: [[shared.oneapi.write-practices:activation-zia-cbc]].

prose.label: Everywhere else.
prose.text: {{object-activate-paths}} {{no-other-gate}} When a write in those products takes effect is not documented: [[shared.oneapi.write-practices:other-products-no-activation]], and for ZPA [[zpa.api.activation]].

prose.label: ZIA.
prose.text: Saving versus activating, the status values and the activate call are in [[zia.api.activation]]. The platform also activates when an admin or API session ends, and a queued activation publishes every pending change in the tenant: [[zia.terraform.activation-methods]]. How the Terraform provider and the Python SDK trigger activation is in [[zia.terraform.activation]], [[zia.terraform.activation-resource]] and [[zia.sdk-python.activation-and-session]].

prose.label: Cloud & Branch Connector.
prose.text: The activate and forced-activate calls and the Terraform resource are in [[cloud-connector.api.activation-wire]], and the guide's POST against the contract's PUT is [[shared.oneapi.write-practices:cbc-activate-method]]. Its status read uses a different vocabulary from ZIA's: [[shared.activation.cbc]].

prose.label: Writes refused before activation.
prose.text: An edit-lock 409 and the maintenance read-only 403 stop a write before anything is staged: [[shared.oneapi.write-practices:edit-lock-409]], [[shared.oneapi.response-codes:read-only-mode]], [[shared.oneapi.response-codes:read-only-distinguishable]]. The ZIA clients' retries on the lock are in [[zia.api.rate-limits:zia-edit-lock-retry]] and [[zia.terraform.activation-methods:lock-errors-retried]].

prose.label: Failures and tooling.
prose.text: Why an activation fails and what then stays staged is open {{gap:activation-failure}}, and so is how long the in-progress state lasts {{gap:inprogress-duration}}. {{mcp-zia-only}}

checks.do: Which product the change was made in: only ZIA and Cloud & Branch Connector changes wait for an activation.
For ZIA, the activation status, and whether a session end has already activated the change.
For Cloud & Branch Connector, the organization edit status and the per-admin activation states, not a PENDING value.
Whether an activation queued behind other editing sessions, which cannot be cancelled, explains the delay.
Whether the write was refused with an edit-lock 409 or a maintenance 403 and never staged.
Whether a Terraform run created the activation resource after the last change.

object-activate-paths.statement: Other products' API specifications have activate operations that act on one object: the ZCC web policy activate enables or disables a policy or app profile for a platform, the ZDX application activate activates one application by its ID, and the ZPA emergency-access activate activates one emergency access user.

expect.description: Enables or disables a policy or app profile for the company by platform (iOS, Android, Windows, macOS, and Linux).
Activates a specific application by its ID.
Activates the emergency access user for the specified customer.

no-other-gate.statement: Outside ZIA and Cloud & Branch Connector the captured API specifications have no call that activates staged configuration for the organization, so a saved change in ZPA, ZCC, ZDX or ZIdentity has no activation step to check.
no-other-gate.conditions: Rests on a search of every captured OneAPI specification (ZIA, ZPA, ZCC, ZDX, Cloud & Branch Connector, ZIdentity, Unified RBAC, BI, EASM, Cellular, Event Monitoring, AI Guard, AI Security) for paths containing 'activat': only ZIA and Cloud & Branch Connector have an organization-wide activate, and the remaining matches act on one object. Absence of an activation call does not establish when a write in those products takes effect (gap shared.oneapi.write-practices:other-products-no-activation).

mcp-zia-only.statement: The MCP server implements a ZIA activation-status tool and a ZIA activate tool, and its Cloud & Branch Connector tool modules include no activation tool.

quotes: Activate staged ZIA configuration changes (write). Run after any ZIA write.

mcp-zia-only.conditions: The Cloud & Branch Connector absence rests on listing src/zscaler_mcp/tools/ztw at the pin: account details, discovery service, IP destination, IP and IP source groups, admins, roles, network service groups, network services and public cloud info.

activation-failure.title: Why an activation fails and what stays staged
activation-failure.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "If a pending change exceeds a ranges-and-limitations ceiling or fails server-side validation, activation may fail with a specific error. The config remains staged; fix the offending resource and re-activate." No captured source describes activation failures, their errors, or whether the staged configuration survives one. The Cloud & Branch Connector status carries an ADM_ACTV_FAIL admin state without a description.
activation-failure.blocks: diagnosing an activation call that returned an error

inprogress-duration.title: How long ZIA reports INPROGRESS
inprogress-duration.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "INPROGRESS: Activation is currently running (transient; should clear within seconds-to-minutes)"; scripts should poll until ACTIVE or PENDING. The specification lists INPROGRESS as a status value without a duration or polling guidance.
inprogress-duration.blocks: choosing a polling interval and timeout after an activate call
